firstMoves.label: 1.b3
firstMoves.hint: Larsen: bishop on the long diagonal

openings.name: Italian Game: Giuoco Piano
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5
openings.summary: The bishop eyes f7. Develop naturally, castle fast and build slowly with c3 and d3.

lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O-O Nbd2 a6 Bb3 Ba7 h3
lines.idea: No rush: route the knight via f1 to g3 and break with d4 when you are ready.

lines.name: Pianissimo with ...a6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 a6 O-O d6 Bb3 Ba7 Nbd2 O-O h3
lines.idea: Bb3 dodges ...Na5, and h3 takes g4 away from Black's pieces.

lines.name: Early ...d6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb6 Nc3 Nf6 O-O
lines.idea: If Black delays ...Nf6, claim the full centre at once.

openings.name: Evans Gambit
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4
openings.summary: Kasparov's surprise weapon. Give a pawn to win time for c3 and d4 and a huge attack.

lines.name: Accepted with ...Ba5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 exd4 O-O d6 cxd4 Bb6 Nc3
lines.idea: Your centre and development are worth far more than the pawn.

lines.name: Accepted with ...Be7
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Be7 d4 Na5 Be2 exd4 Qxd4
lines.idea: Save the bishop, then use the queen in the centre to hit g7.

lines.name: Declined
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bb6 a4 a6 Nc3 Nf6 Nd5
lines.idea: a4 gains space with tempo threats, and Nd5 hits the b6 bishop.

openings.name: Fried Liver Attack (Two Knights)
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5
openings.summary: The most famous attack in club chess. Everyone falls for it at least once.

lines.name: Fried Liver
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+ Ke6 Nc3
lines.idea: Sacrifice the knight to drag the king out. Pile up on the pinned d5 knight.

lines.name: Polerio Defence
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5+ c6 dxc6 bxc6 Be2 h6 Nf3 e4 Ne5
lines.idea: You keep an extra pawn. Stay calm: Black has activity, not a win.

lines.name: Traxler Counterattack
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7+ Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 O-O d6 c3
lines.idea: Do not get greedy with Nxf7. Take with the bishop and keep your king safe.

lines.name: Fritz Variation
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nd4 c3 b5 Bf1 Nxd5 cxd4 Qxg5 Bxb5+
lines.idea: Win a tempo on the knight and collect material on the way out.

openings.name: Italian Game: Two Knights with d3
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3
openings.summary: Skip the Fried Liver theory and get a calm, rich Italian structure.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 c3 d6 O-O O-O Nbd2 a6 Bb3 Ba7 h3
lines.idea: Same plan as the Pianissimo: Re1, Nf1 and Ng3.

lines.name: With ...Be7
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Be7 O-O O-O Re1 d6 c3 Na5 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bc2
lines.idea: Keep your bishop when ...Na5 hunts it.

lines.name: With ...d5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-O Be7 Re1 O-O Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 Nb6 Bb3
lines.idea: Black's e5 pawn is loose. Your rook on e1 makes Nxe5 work and you win it.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez: Main Lines
openings.summary: Five hundred years old and still a favourite of world champions. Slow pressure on e5.

lines.name: Closed
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3
lines.idea: c3 and h3 prepare d4 with no ...Bg4 pin. The bishop stays on the a2-g8 diagonal.

lines.name: Open
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 b5 Bb3 d5 dxe5 Be6 c3
lines.idea: No hurry to win the pawn back. Open lines while Black's king is still in the centre.

lines.name: Berlin
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bxc6 dxc6 dxe5 Nf5 Qxd8+ Kxd8
lines.idea: A queenless middlegame. Your kingside pawn majority is the long-term trump.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5 Ne4 O-O d5
lines.idea: c3 and d4 hit the c5 bishop and win central time.

lines.name: Steinitz
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bd7 Nc3 Nf6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: ...d6 is passive, so open the centre and enjoy extra space.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6
openings.summary: Fischer's pet line. Damage Black's pawns and steer for an endgame you can win on autopilot.

lines.name: Main line with ...f6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O f6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 c5 Nb3 Qxd1 Rxd1
lines.idea: Trade queens. Your kingside majority can make a passed pawn, Black's cannot.

lines.name: With ...Bg4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O Bg4 h3 h5 d3 Qf6 Nbd2
lines.idea: Do not take on g4: the open h-file would help Black.

lines.name: With ...Qd6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O Qd6 Na3 b5 c3
lines.idea: Black wants ...O-O-O. Na3 and d4 keep the initiative.

openings.name: Scotch Game
openings.summary: Blow the centre open on move three. Active pieces and far less theory than the Ruy Lopez.

lines.name: Mieses
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Qe7 Qe2 Nd5 c4
lines.idea: Double the pawns on c6, then kick the knight with e5 and c4.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c3 Nge7 Bc4
lines.idea: Be3 and c3 hold d4 against everything Black piles on it.

lines.name: Early knight trade
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 d6 Bc4 Nf6 Nc3 Be7 O-O
lines.idea: A centralised queen that cannot easily be chased. Develop with tempo.

openings.name: Scotch Gambit
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4
openings.summary: Skip the recapture and aim straight at f7. Full of traps at club level.

lines.name: With ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4 Nf6 e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4 Nxd4 Bd7 Bxc6 bxc6 O-O
lines.idea: e5 kicks the knight and Bb5 keeps the pressure on c6.

lines.name: With ...Bc5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2 Nxd2 Nbxd2
lines.idea: c3 opens the position and you keep a strong pawn centre.

openings.name: Four Knights: Spanish
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6
openings.summary: Classical, symmetrical and easy to play. Great for learning how to develop.

lines.name: Symmetrical
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O d3 d6 Bg5 Bxc3 bxc3
lines.idea: The pin on f6 is annoying. Black copying you for long is risky.

lines.name: Rubinstein
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 e5 dxc3 exf6 Qxf6 dxc3 Qe5+ Qe2
lines.idea: Forcing play that leaves you with a small but safe plus.

lines.name: With ...Bd6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Bb5 Bd6 O-O O-O d3 h6 Re1
lines.idea: ...Bd6 blocks Black's own d-pawn, so simply develop and play d4 later.

openings.name: Ponziani Opening
openings.summary: An old-school surprise. Prepare d4 at once and catch unprepared opponents.

lines.name: With ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 d5 Ne7 Nxe5 Ng6 Qd4 Qf6 Nxg6
lines.idea: Gain time on the knights and use your space advantage.

lines.name: With ...d5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 c3 d5 Qa4 f6 Bb5 Ne7 exd5 Qxd5 O-O
lines.idea: Qa4 and Bb5 pin the c6 knight, so Black's e5 stays under fire.

openings.name: Vienna Game
openings.summary: A King's Gambit with better timing. Develop a knight first, then hit e5 with f4.

lines.name: Vienna Gambit
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 Nf3 Be7 d4 O-O Bd3
lines.idea: A big pawn on e5 cramps Black and your pieces aim at the king.

lines.name: With ...Nc6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ng5 h6 Nxf7
lines.idea: The Hamppe-Allgaier: a wild piece sacrifice to expose the king.

lines.name: With ...Bc5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Bg5 h6 Bh4
lines.idea: Grab the centre and pin the f6 knight.

openings.name: King's Gambit
openings.summary: The romantic opening of the 1800s. Sacrifice a pawn to rip open the f-file.

lines.name: Kieseritzky
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 Bd6 d4
lines.idea: h4 breaks the pawn chain and Ne5 plants a monster knight.

lines.name: Fischer Defence
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6 d4 g5 h4 g4 Ng1 Bh6 Nc3
lines.idea: The knight's retreat is real: you will win back f4 and keep the centre.

lines.name: Declined
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 Bc5 Nf3 d6 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3
lines.idea: The c5 bishop stops you castling. Prepare Na4 to remove it.

lines.name: Falkbeer
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxd5 O-O
lines.idea: Castle quickly and pressure the d5 knight along the open lines.

openings.name: Bishop's Opening
openings.summary: Bishop first keeps your f-pawn free and sidesteps the Petrov. Beloved by Philidor.

lines.name: Berlin Defence
lines.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d3 c6 Nf3 d5 Bb3 Bd6 Nc3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Let Black take the centre, then undermine it from the sides.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Nc3
lines.idea: c3 and d4 win the centre and gain time on the bishop.

lines.name: With ...Nc6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6 c3
lines.idea: Transposes into a comfortable Italian.

openings.name: Danish Gambit
openings.summary: Give up two pawns for two raking bishops. A scary attack on move six.

lines.name: Double Gambit
lines.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Bc4 cxb2 Bxb2 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bxf7+ Kxf7 Qxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Bxd2+ Nxd2
lines.idea: If Black returns material properly the game levels out. Everyone else gets mated.

lines.name: Sörensen Defence
lines.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 cxd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Bb4+ Nc3
lines.idea: An isolated pawn but active pieces. Develop and use the d5 outpost.

openings.name: Center Game
openings.summary: Bring the queen out early and castle long. A provocative, unusual fight.

lines.name: Paulsen Attack
lines.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qe3 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 O-O O-O-O Re8 Qg3
lines.idea: Qg3 prepares the attack on the kingside once you have castled long.

openings.name: Beating the Petrov & Stafford
openings.summary: Take on e5 with confidence. Know the Stafford traps and walk away a pawn up.

lines.name: Classical Petrov
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3 Nc6 O-O Be7 c4
lines.idea: Hit the e4 knight's support with c4 and keep a small, lasting edge.

lines.name: Stafford Gambit
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5 c3 Ng4 d4
lines.idea: Do not touch g4 with your bishop. d3 and Be2 defuse the Bxf2 tricks.

lines.name: Damiano-style blunder
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Qe7 d4 d6 Nf3 Qxe4+ Be2
lines.idea: Black wins the pawn back but falls behind. Develop with tempo.

openings.name: Beating the Philidor
openings.summary: Black plays passively from move two. Take space and keep it.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Be7 Bf4 O-O Qd2
lines.idea: Set up Bf4, Qd2 and O-O-O. You have space and a free hand on the kingside.

lines.name: Hanham
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7 Bc4 Be7 O-O O-O a4
lines.idea: a4 secures the bishop's home. Black is cramped, so avoid trades.

openings.name: Beating the Latvian Gambit
openings.summary: Black's wildest second move. Learn the refutation and enjoy the extra tempo.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Nxe5 Qf6 d4 d6 Nc4 fxe4 Nc3 Qg6 f3
lines.idea: f3 breaks the pawn chain. Your pieces all come out fast.

lines.name: With ...Nc6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Nxe5 Nc6 Qh5+ g6 Nxg6 Nf6 Qh4 hxg6 Qxh8
lines.idea: Qh5+ and Nxg6 punish ...Nc6 at once, and you pick up the rook on h8.

openings.name: Beating the Elephant Gambit
openings.summary: It looks scary but is unsound. Take the pawn and pin the e-file.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 e4 Qe2 Nf6 d3 Qxd5 Nbd2 Be7 dxe4
lines.idea: Qe2 pins the e-pawn. Bring your pieces out and you stay a pawn up.

lines.name: With ...Bd6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Bd6 d4 e4 Ne5 Nf6 Nc3 O-O Be2
lines.idea: Ne5 lands in the centre and the d5 pawn stays yours.

openings.name: Open Sicilian
openings.summary: The critical try against 1...c5. Open the centre and go for the king.

lines.name: English Attack vs Najdorf
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O O-O-O
lines.idea: Castle long and storm with g4 and h4. Opposite-side castling is a race.

lines.name: Yugoslav vs Dragon
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7 O-O-O
lines.idea: Trade the dark bishop with Bh6 and open the h-file. Sac, sac, mate.

lines.name: Against ...e5 (Sveshnikov)
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Ndb5 d6 Bg5 a6 Na3 b5 Nd5
lines.idea: Black has a hole on d5, and your knight wants to live there forever.

lines.name: Against ...e6
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Qc7 Be3 a6 Bd3 Nf6 O-O
lines.idea: Develop classically, then play f4 and Qe1-g3 to attack.

lines.name: Against the Kan
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6 Nc3 Qc7 Bd3 Nf6 O-O
lines.idea: A sturdy setup. The bishop on d3 points at the king.

openings.name: Alapin Sicilian
openings.summary: Skip mountains of Sicilian theory with one quiet pawn move, then build a big centre.

lines.name: With ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 Nf3 Nc6 cxd4 d6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb5
lines.idea: Gain space with tempo. Recapture on d4 with the pawn for a classical centre.

lines.name: With ...d5
lines.moves: e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Nc6 Be3
lines.idea: Black's queen comes out early, so develop and hit it with c4 or Nc3.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: e4 c5 c3 e6 d4 d5 e5 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3
lines.idea: This is a French Advance structure. a3 and b4 expand with tempo.

openings.name: Smith-Morra Gambit
openings.summary: A pawn for a lightning fast attack. The scourge of online blitz.

lines.name: Accepted
lines.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 Bc4 e6 O-O Nf6 Qe2 Be7 Rd1
lines.idea: Every piece on its best square, with rooks on c1 and d1. Watch the Nd5 and e5 breaks.

lines.name: Declined with ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 cxd4 d6 Bc4
lines.idea: You get an Alapin with your bishop already active.

lines.name: Declined with ...d3
lines.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 d3 Bxd3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 c4
lines.idea: Black gives the pawn back. c4 builds a Maroczy bind.

openings.name: Grand Prix Attack
openings.summary: A club player's favourite. Launch f4, f5 and go for mate without Sicilian theory.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Bc4 e6 f5 Nge7 fxe6 dxe6 d3
lines.idea: Pry open the f-file. Your bishop on c4 and rook on f1 aim at f7.

lines.name: With ...d6
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 d6 f4 Nc6 Nf3 g6 Bc4 Bg7 O-O e6 f5
lines.idea: Same plan: open lines with f5 and swing the queen to e1 and h4.

openings.name: Closed Sicilian
openings.summary: Keep the centre shut and play on the kingside. Spassky's choice.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6 f4 e6 Nf3 Nge7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Build slowly with f4 and Be3, then attack on the kingside.

openings.name: Rossolimo & Moscow Sicilian
openings.summary: The grandmaster way to avoid the Najdorf: Bb5 instead of d4.

lines.name: Rossolimo with ...g6
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 g6 O-O Bg7 Re1 e5 Bxc6 dxc6 d3 Qc7 Nc3
lines.idea: Give up the bishop to wreck the pawns, then aim for f4 or Nd5.

lines.name: Rossolimo with ...e6
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 e6 O-O Nge7 Re1 a6 Bf1 d5 exd5 Nxd5 d4
lines.idea: Pull back the bishop to keep it, and open the centre with d4.

lines.name: Moscow
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+ Bd7 Bxd7+ Qxd7 O-O Nc6 c3 Nf6 Re1 e6 d4
lines.idea: Trade bishops and build a pawn centre with c3 and d4.

lines.name: Against ...e6
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 c3 d5 e5 Nc6 d4 Qb6 a3
lines.idea: Avoid the open lines and steer for a French Advance structure.

openings.name: Beating the Caro-Kann: Advance
openings.summary: Grab space with e5 and aim for Black's bishop on f5.

lines.name: Short System
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nd7 O-O Ne7 Nbd2 h6 Nb3
lines.idea: Quiet and strong. Nb3 keeps c5 under control and c3 holds the centre.

lines.name: Against ...c5
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 e6 Be3 Nd7 Nf3 Nxc5 Be2
lines.idea: Take the pawn and use the d4 square.

openings.name: Beating the Caro-Kann: Exchange
openings.prefix: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3
openings.summary: A Carlsbad structure with reversed colours: easy plans and a safe king.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3 Qd7 Nd2 e6 Ngf3
lines.idea: Qb3 hits b7 and d5. You have the easier development.

openings.name: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation
openings.summary: One strange pawn move, instant chaos. Your e4 pawn stays and Black's plans fall apart.

lines.name: With ...dxe4
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 exd4 Bc4 Bb4+ c3
lines.idea: Black's strike at d4 lets you gambit a pawn for very fast development.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Be3 Bb4 Qd3
lines.idea: Hold e4 solidly, and the f3 pawn turns out to be useful after all.

lines.name: With ...g6
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Be3 Nf6 Qd2 O-O O-O-O
lines.idea: Castle long and go for an attack with h4.

openings.name: Beating the French: Advance
openings.summary: Lock the centre and squeeze. Black's light-squared bishop becomes a spectator.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 Bd7 b4 cxd4 cxd4
lines.idea: a3 and b4 stake out queenside space. Hold d4 and attack on the kingside.

lines.name: With ...Nh6
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 Nh6 b4 cxd4 cxd4 Nf5 Bb2
lines.idea: Protect d4 with the bishop, then trade the f5 knight.

openings.name: Beating the French: Tarrasch
openings.summary: Nd2 avoids the Winawer pin and keeps your c-pawn free. Karpov's choice.

lines.name: Open with ...c5
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 exd5 exd5 Ngf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bd6 dxc5 Bxc5 O-O Ne7 Nb3 Bd6
lines.idea: Black has an isolated pawn. Blockade d4 and trade minor pieces.

lines.name: With ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Ne2 cxd4 cxd4
lines.idea: A pawn chain with a kingside attack. Ne2 supports d4 and leaves f-file options.

lines.name: Rubinstein with ...dxe4
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Nf3 Ngf6 Nxf6+ Nxf6 Bd3
lines.idea: You have free piece play and more central space.

openings.name: Beating the Scandinavian
openings.summary: Develop while chasing the queen around the board.

lines.name: ...Qa5 main line
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 c6 Bc4 Bf5 Bd2 e6 Nd5 Qd8 Nxf6+ Qxf6
lines.idea: Win tempi on the queen and take the bishop pair where possible.

lines.name: ...Qd6
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6 Nf3 a6 g3
lines.idea: A fianchetto is best against the d6 queen setup.

lines.name: Modern with ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5 Nf3 g6 c4 Nb6 Nc3 Bg7 h3
lines.idea: Take the centre. Black's knight on b6 is badly placed.

openings.name: Beating the Alekhine
openings.summary: Chase the knight, grab the space, and do not overextend.

lines.name: Modern
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Be7 c4 Nb6 Nc3 O-O
lines.idea: Simple development beats Black's provocations. Your space is real.

lines.name: With ...dxe5
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 dxe5 Nxe5 c6 Be2 Bf5 O-O Nd7 Nf3
lines.idea: Black is solid but passive. You keep the extra space.

openings.name: Pirc: Austrian Attack
openings.prefix: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4
openings.summary: Three pawns abreast roll at the king. The critical test of the Pirc.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Bd3 Na6 O-O c5 d5
lines.idea: Close the centre with d5, then play Qe1-h4 and f5.

lines.name: With ...c5
lines.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Bb5+ Bd7 e5
lines.idea: A check first, then e5. Black is in real danger.

openings.name: Beating the Modern Defence
openings.summary: Black gives you the whole centre. Take it with the 150 Attack.

lines.name: 150 Attack
lines.moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 Be3 a6 Qd2 b5 f3 Nd7 h4
lines.idea: Named for the 150 BCF rating of the English players who used it. Be3, Qd2, h4.

lines.name: With ...c6
lines.moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 c6 Be3 d5 Qd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ Bxf6 O-O-O
lines.idea: Castle long, then push h4.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit
openings.summary: Yes, the one from the show. Offer a pawn to take the centre, with lasting pressure.

lines.name: Declined
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 b6 Bd3
lines.idea: The pin on f6 hurts, and Black's c8 bishop is shut in.

lines.name: Slav
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O
lines.idea: a4 stops ...b5, and you win back c4 with a lead in development.

lines.name: Semi-Slav
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Qc2 Bd6 Be2 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Qc2 prepares the e4 break, your central plan.

lines.name: Accepted
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O a6 a4
lines.idea: No hurry for the pawn: e3 and Bxc4 win it back with the centre in hand.

lines.name: Albin Countergambit
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Be6 Nbd2 Qd7 Bg2
lines.idea: Give the pawn back if needed: the fianchetto hits the queenside.

lines.name: Chigorin
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Bxf3 gxf3 Qxd5 e3 e5 Nc3
lines.idea: You get the bishop pair. Open the position for them.

openings.name: Catalan Opening
openings.summary: Kramnik's and Carlsen's weapon. The g2 bishop slowly crushes the queenside.

lines.name: Open
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 Be7 Nf3 O-O O-O dxc4 Qc2 a6 a4 Bd7 Qxc4
lines.idea: Win the c4 pawn back and the long diagonal becomes a laser.

lines.name: Bogo-style check
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 Bb4+ Bd2 Be7 Bg2 d5 Nf3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Black's bishop lost time returning home.

lines.name: With ...c5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 c5 Nf3 cxd4 Nxd4 d5 Bg2 e5 Nf3
lines.idea: Black takes space, but you get great play on the long diagonal.

openings.name: Beating the Nimzo-Indian
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3
openings.summary: The Rubinstein: solid development and a real plan against the bishop pin.

lines.name: With ...O-O and ...d5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 O-O Bd3 d5 Nf3 c5 O-O Nc6 a3 Bxc3 bxc3
lines.idea: You get the bishop pair and a central pawn mass.

lines.name: With ...b6
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 b6 Bd3 Bb7 Nf3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Develop first, then use the e4 break.

lines.name: With ...c5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 c5 Bd3 Nc6 Nf3 d5 O-O
lines.idea: Natural setup. The c3 knight stays pinned, not doubled, for now.

openings.name: Beating the King's Indian
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4
openings.summary: Win the race: queenside attack against Black's kingside storm.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7 Ne1
lines.idea: Close the centre, then push c5. Black races with ...f5.

lines.name: With ...Nbd7
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nbd7 Re1 c6 Bf1
lines.idea: Keep the tension: Black's e5 pawn and d6 pawn can become targets.

lines.name: With ...c5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 c5 O-O cxd4 Nxd4
lines.idea: A Maroczy-type bind. You are squeezing, not attacking.

openings.name: Beating the Grünfeld
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
openings.summary: Take the whole centre. Then find out if it was a good idea.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Rb1 O-O Be2
lines.idea: Rb1 pre-empts ...Bg4 trades and pressures b7. Keep your centre protected.

openings.name: Beating the Benoni & Benko
openings.summary: Black's dynamic counterattacks. Accept the pawn or crash through in the centre.

lines.name: Modern Benoni
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 e4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Be2 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Your e5 break is the whole game. Prepare it with Nd2 and f4.

lines.name: Benko Gambit
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6 Bxa6 Nc3 d6 e4 Bxf1 Kxf1
lines.idea: Take everything and your king is fine. You are a healthy pawn up.

openings.name: London System
openings.summary: The same setup against almost everything: d4, Bf4, e3, Nf3, c3, Nbd2. Almost no theory.

lines.name: Against ...d5 and ...c5
lines.moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nd2 e6 Ngf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3
lines.idea: If Black trades on g3 your structure is still rock solid. Aim for Ne5.

lines.name: Against early ...e6
lines.moves: d4 d5 Bf4 e6 e3 Nf6 Nf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2
lines.idea: Bg3 preserves the bishop against ...Bd6.

lines.name: Against ...Bf5
lines.moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Nf6 Nf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Nbd2
lines.idea: Simplify with Bd3. The trade leaves you well developed.

lines.name: Against the King's Indian
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 e3 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Be2 d6 h3 Nbd7 O-O
lines.idea: h3 gives your bishop a retreat and stops ...Ng4 and ...Bg4.

lines.name: Against ...e6 and ...c5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3 c5 c3 d5 Nd2 Nc6 Ngf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3
lines.idea: You end up in the same setup. That is the beauty of the system.

lines.name: Against 1...e6
lines.moves: d4 e6 Bf4 d5 e3 Nf6 Nf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2
lines.idea: Move order does not matter. Pieces go to the same squares.

lines.name: Against 1...g6
lines.moves: d4 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6 Nf3 Nf6 Be2 O-O h3 Nbd7 O-O
lines.idea: Same scheme: h3, castle, then c4 or Nbd2.

openings.name: Jobava London
openings.summary: The London's aggressive cousin. Nc3 and Bf4 set up Nb5 threats from move three.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 a6 Nf3 Nc6 Bd3
lines.idea: A symmetrical pawn structure, but your pieces land first. Ne5 and Qf3 come next.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4 e6 Nb5 Na6 e3 Be7 Nf3 O-O Bd3
lines.idea: Nb5 forces Black's knight to the rim.

lines.name: With ...Bf5
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Bf5 Bf4 e6 e3 Nf6 Nb5 Na6 a3
lines.idea: Keep the b5 knight there as a thorn.

openings.name: Richter-Veresov Attack
openings.summary: Hit f6 and follow up with f3 and e4: a rarely prepared attacking setup.

lines.name: With ...Nbd7
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3 h6 Bh4 e6 e3 Be7 Bd3
lines.idea: Develop, castle, then break with e4.

lines.name: With ...Bf5
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Bf5 f3 Nbd7 Nxd5 Nxd5 e4
lines.idea: A tactical shot wins back the piece with a big centre.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 e6 e4 dxe4 Nxe4 Be7 Bxf6 Bxf6 Nf3
lines.idea: e4 at once gives you a free French-like position.

openings.name: Trompowsky Attack
openings.summary: Black's second move is already an awkward decision. A favourite of Carlsen in rapid.

lines.name: With ...Ne4
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4 c5 f3 Qa5+ c3 Nf6 d5
lines.idea: Kick the knight and build a big centre with d5.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 e6 e4 h6 Bxf6 Qxf6 Nc3 d6 Qd2
lines.idea: Give up the bishop for development and a big pawn centre.

lines.name: With ...d5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 d5 Bxf6 exf6 e3 Bd6 c4 dxc4 Bxc4
lines.idea: Black's doubled pawns restrict their bishops.

lines.name: With ...c5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 c5 d5 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Bd2 Qb6 e4
lines.idea: A gambit for a strong centre and fast development.

openings.name: Torre Attack
openings.summary: Bg5 with no c4. Simple development with a quiet kingside attack in mind.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bh4 c5 e3 Be7 Nbd2 b6 Bd3
lines.idea: Hold the pin as long as you can and play c3 and e4.

lines.name: With ...g6
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bg5 Bg7 Nbd2 d6 c3 O-O e4
lines.idea: e4 gives you a real centre with very little effort.

lines.name: With ...d5
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bg5 e6 e3 Be7 Bd3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: A calm setup. Trade on f6 at the right moment.

openings.name: Colle-Zukertort System
openings.summary: Set up, castle, and aim two bishops at the king. Easy to learn and dangerous.

lines.name: Zukertort setup
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bd3 c5 b3 Nc6 O-O Bd6 Bb2 O-O Nbd2
lines.idea: Plant a knight on e5, then swing a rook or queen over to the kingside.

lines.name: Against ...Bg4
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bg4 c4 e6 Nc3 Nbd7 h3 Bh5
lines.idea: With the bishop outside, c4 and Qb3 hit the weakened b7.

lines.name: Against ...Bf5
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Bd3 e6 Bxf5 exf5 Qd3
lines.idea: Trade the bishop and hit the doubled f-pawns with Qd3.

openings.name: Stonewall Attack
openings.summary: Pawns on c3, d4, e3, f4 and a fast attack with Bd3, Ne5. Beginners love it.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 f4 Bg4 Nf3 e6 O-O Bd6
lines.idea: Ne5 next, then Qe1-h4. Once the knight lands, the attack plays itself.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: d4 d5 e3 e6 Bd3 Nf6 f4 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Bd6 O-O
lines.idea: Black has not stopped the plan, so carry on with Ne5 and Qe1.

openings.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
openings.summary: 1.d4 for attackers. Give a pawn and go after the king on the f-file.

lines.name: Bogoljubov Defence
lines.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 g6 Bc4 Bg7 O-O O-O Qe1
lines.idea: Qe1-h4 then Bh6. Your rook on f1 joins in.

lines.name: Euwe Defence
lines.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 e6 Bg5 Be7 Bd3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Every piece is pointed at the kingside. Look for Ne5 and Qe1.

lines.name: Ziegler Defence
lines.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 c6 Bc4 Bf5 O-O e6 Qe1
lines.idea: Same recipe. Keep your rook on the f-file and press f7.

lines.name: Lemberger Countergambit
lines.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 e5 dxe5 Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nfd7 Nd5 Kd8 Bg5+ f6 exf6 gxf6
lines.idea: Take on e5, trade queens, then Nd5 and Bg5+ exploit the loose black king.

openings.name: Beating the Dutch
openings.summary: Fianchetto first and let Black overextend on the kingside.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: d4 f5 Nf3 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O c4 d5 b3
lines.idea: b3 and Ba3 trade Black's good bishop in the Stonewall.

lines.name: Leningrad
lines.moves: d4 f5 Nf3 Nf6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 O-O O-O c4 d6 Nc3
lines.idea: Stop ...e5 for as long as you can with d5 and Qc2.

openings.name: Staunton Gambit
openings.summary: Punish the Dutch immediately by opening up the weakened king.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 g6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Pour your pieces toward the kingside. Qd2 and Bh6 will follow.

lines.name: With ...c6
lines.moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 c6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 d5 Bd3
lines.idea: Black is solid but behind in development. Castle and play Ne5.

openings.name: Beating the Englund Gambit
openings.prefix: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7
openings.summary: A notorious blitz trap. Learn the one move that avoids Qc1 mate.

lines.name: Avoid the trap
lines.moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Nc3 Bb4 Rb1 Qa3 Nd5
lines.idea: Never Bc3?, Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1 mate. Nc3 and Rb1 turn the tables.

openings.name: Réti Opening
openings.summary: Hypermodern chess. Attack the centre from afar and let Black overreach.

lines.name: With ...e6
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 c4 e6 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O b3 c5 Bb2 Nc6 e3
lines.idea: A double fianchetto sweeps both long diagonals.

lines.name: With ...c6
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 c4 c6 b3 Nf6 g3 Bf5 Bg2 e6 Bb2 Nbd7 O-O
lines.idea: The bishops look across the board at Black's position.

lines.name: With ...d4
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 c4 d4 e3 Nc6 exd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 Nc3
lines.idea: Undermine the pawn, trade and gain time on the queen.

lines.name: With ...dxc4
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 e6 O-O c5 b3
lines.idea: You win the pawn back and have a central majority.

openings.name: King's Indian Attack
openings.summary: Bobby Fischer's system. One setup against anything, then a kingside attack.

lines.name: Against ...d5 and ...c5
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 c5 O-O Nc6 d3 e5 Nbd2 Be7 e4 O-O
lines.idea: Build with Re1 and e5, and push h4 and Nf1 to attack.

lines.name: Against ...Bf5
lines.moves: Nf3 d5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Bf5 O-O e6 d3 h6 Nbd2 Be7 Qe1 O-O e4
lines.idea: Qe1 prepares e4 with tempo on the bishop.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6 and ...g6
lines.moves: Nf3 Nf6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 O-O O-O d3 d6 e4
lines.idea: A reversed King's Indian: keep the tension and prepare your break.

lines.name: Against ...c5
lines.moves: Nf3 c5 g3 Nc6 Bg2 g6 O-O Bg7 d3 d6 e4
lines.idea: A closed Sicilian structure. Plan c3 and d4.

lines.name: Against ...e6
lines.moves: Nf3 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O Be7 d3 O-O Nbd2 c5 e4
lines.idea: This is the classic French version of the KIA.

openings.name: English Opening
openings.summary: Control d5 from the side and aim the g2 bishop. Perfect if you prefer plans to theory.

lines.name: Reversed Sicilian
lines.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2 Nb6 O-O Be7 d3
lines.idea: It is a Sicilian with an extra tempo. The g2 bishop owns the diagonal.

lines.name: With ...Bb4
lines.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Bb4 Bg2 O-O O-O e4 Ng5 Bxc3 bxc3 Re8 f3
lines.idea: Give up the structure to gain the centre with f3 and the f-file.

lines.name: Symmetrical
lines.moves: c4 c5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 O-O O-O d3 d6 a3
lines.idea: You move first: a3 and b4 give you the queenside initiative.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6 and ...e6
lines.moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 d5 d4 Be7 Bg5 O-O e3 h6 Bh4
lines.idea: Transposes to a Queen's Gambit Declined if Black agrees.

lines.name: Against the King's Indian
lines.moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 g3 Bg7 Bg2 O-O Nf3 d6 O-O e5 d3
lines.idea: Fianchetto and d3: control d5 and prepare Rb1 and b4.

lines.name: Against 1...e6
lines.moves: c4 e6 Nc3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bg5 O-O e3 h6 Bh4
lines.idea: Go into a Queen's Gambit with your pieces well placed.

lines.name: Against 1...g6
lines.moves: c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 g3 d6 Bg2 e5 d3 Nf6 Nf3 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Same scheme: g3, Bg2, d3, Nf3 and castle.

lines.name: Against 1...c6
lines.moves: c4 c6 Nf3 d5 e3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 d4 Nbd7 Qc2 Bd6 Be2 O-O O-O
lines.idea: If Black goes Slav, set up e3, Qc2 and Be2.

openings.name: Bird's Opening
openings.summary: A reversed Dutch with an extra tempo: control e5 and swing to the kingside.

lines.name: Leningrad setup
lines.moves: f4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e3 g6 Be2 Bg7 O-O O-O d3 c5 Qe1
lines.idea: Qe1-h4 starts your attack, and e4 is the break to prepare.

lines.name: From's Gambit
lines.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 exd6 Bxd6 Nf3 g5 g3 g4 Nh4
lines.idea: Take the pawn but be careful. Do not fall for Qh4+ and mate on g3.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6
lines.moves: f4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 e3 Bg7 Be2 O-O O-O d6 d3
lines.idea: A flexible setup. Plan Qe1 and e4.

lines.name: Against ...c5
lines.moves: f4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 e3 g6 Be2 Bg7 O-O d6 d3
lines.idea: Same scheme, and Qe1 stays your main idea.

openings.name: Larsen's Opening
openings.summary: Nimzowitsch-Larsen: fianchetto on move two and pressure e5 from the very start.

lines.name: Against ...e5
lines.moves: b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 e3 d5 Bb5 Bd6 f4
lines.idea: Bb5 and f4 both attack the e5 pawn's support.

lines.name: Against ...d5
lines.moves: b3 d5 Bb2 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Be7 Be2 O-O O-O
lines.idea: A quiet Queen's Indian with colours reversed and an extra tempo.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6
lines.moves: b3 Nf6 Bb2 g6 Bxf6 exf6 c4 Bg7 Nc3 O-O
lines.idea: Wreck the pawns and control d5.

openings.name: Polish Opening (Sokolsky)
openings.summary: The Orangutan. Odd and slightly annoying: the bishop comes to b2 straight away.

lines.name: Against ...e5
lines.moves: b4 e5 Bb2 Bxb4 Bxe5 Nf6 c4 O-O e3 d5 cxd5
lines.idea: You give up a wing pawn to grab a central one. Fair trade.

lines.name: Against ...d5
lines.moves: b4 d5 Bb2 Nf6 e3 e6 a3 Be7 Nf3 O-O c4
lines.idea: a3 supports the b-pawn, and c4 attacks the centre.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6
lines.moves: b4 Nf6 Bb2 e6 a3 d5 e3 Be7 Nf3 O-O c4
lines.idea: Same plan: Bb2, a3, e3, Nf3 and c4.

openings.name: Benko's Opening (Hungarian)
openings.summary: Fianchetto first and decide on the structure later. No theory at all.

lines.name: Against ...d5
lines.moves: g3 d5 Bg2 Nf6 d3 e5 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7 c4
lines.idea: A reversed Pirc or King's Indian. You are a useful tempo up.

lines.name: Against ...e5
lines.moves: g3 e5 Bg2 d5 d3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7 c4
lines.idea: Let Black build the big centre, then strike it with c4.

lines.name: Against ...Nf6
lines.moves: g3 Nf6 Bg2 d5 d3 e5 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7 c4
lines.idea: A reversed King's Indian, and you are a useful tempo up.

openings.name: Grob Attack
openings.summary: Objectively dubious, gloriously chaotic. A meme that wins blitz games.

lines.name: Grob Gambit
lines.moves: g4 d5 Bg2 Bxg4 c4 c6 Qb3 Qd7 cxd5 cxd5 Bxd5
lines.idea: Pressure d5 and b7 at once. Two attackers against one defender wins the pawn back.

lines.name: Against ...e5
lines.moves: g4 e5 Bg2 d5 d3 Nc6 c4 dxc4 dxc4 Qxd1+ Kxd1
lines.idea: Trade the queens and use your bishop on the long diagonal.

openings.name: Sicilian: Najdorf
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
openings.summary: Fischer and Kasparov's weapon. One quiet move, ...a6, and an ocean of possibilities.

lines.name: Against Be2
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5 Nb3 Be7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: ...e5 kicks the knight. Watch out for the hole on d5.

lines.name: English Attack
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O
lines.idea: Counterattack with ...b5 and ...b4 while White attacks on the other flank.

lines.name: Against Bg5
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Be7 Qf3 Qc7 O-O-O Nbd7
lines.idea: ...e6 and ...Be7 hold the pin. Your counterplay is ...b5.

lines.name: Sozin with Bc4
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4 e6 Bb3 b5 O-O Be7
lines.idea: ...e6 blunts the bishop, and ...b5 gains queenside space.

lines.name: Against h3
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 h3 e5 Nde2 h5
lines.idea: ...h5 stops g4 in its tracks.

lines.name: Against f3
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 f3 e5 Nb3 Be6 Be3 h5
lines.idea: Same setup as the English, with ...h5 slowing down g4.

openings.name: Sicilian: Dragon
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
openings.summary: Breathe fire down the long diagonal. Razor-sharp races with opposite-side castling.

lines.name: Yugoslav Attack
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7 O-O-O Rc8 Bb3 Ne5
lines.idea: Pile on c3 and be ready to sacrifice the exchange there.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be2 Bg7 O-O O-O Be3 Nc6
lines.idea: White is less direct, so you get a comfortable game with ...d5 ideas.

lines.name: Levenfish
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Nc6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Nd7
lines.idea: Recapture towards the centre and go after the overextended e5 pawn.

openings.name: Sicilian: Accelerated Dragon
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6
openings.summary: A Dragon without the Yugoslav worry. ...d5 in one go is the dream.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Be3 Nf6 Bc4 O-O Bb3 d6
lines.idea: Trade on d4 and go for ...Bd7 and ...Rc8 on the open file.

lines.name: Maroczy Bind
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 c4 Nf6 Nc3 d6 Be2 Nxd4 Qxd4 Bg7
lines.idea: White has a squeeze, so trade pieces to relieve the cramped position.

openings.name: Sicilian: Sveshnikov
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5
openings.summary: Accept a hole on d5 for active pieces. Carlsen's world championship choice.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Ndb5 d6 Bg5 a6 Na3 b5 Nd5 Be7 Bxf6 Bxf6 c3
lines.idea: The bishop pair and queenside space offset the hole on d5.

lines.name: Against Nf5
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Nf5 d5 exd5 Bxf5 dxc6 bxc6
lines.idea: Hit the centre right away with ...d5.

lines.name: Against Nb3
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Nb3 Bb4 Bd3 d5
lines.idea: A passive retreat lets you get the ...d5 break right away.

openings.name: Sicilian: Taimanov
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6
openings.summary: Flexible and hard to prepare against. Your pieces decide where they go late.

lines.name: English Attack
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Qc7 Be3 a6 Qd2 Nf6 O-O-O Be7
lines.idea: Keep the structure flexible and use ...b5 for counterplay.

lines.name: Against Be2
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Qc7 Be2 a6 O-O Nf6 Be3 Bb4
lines.idea: ...Bb4 pressures e4 and c3.

lines.name: Against Nb5
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6 N1c3 a6 Na3 Be7
lines.idea: A hedgehog structure: wait, then break with ...b5 or ...d5.

openings.name: Sicilian: Kan (Paulsen)
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6
openings.summary: ...a6 and ...Qc7 keep every option open. Excellent counterattacking chances.

lines.name: Against Bd3
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6 Bd3 Nf6 O-O Qc7 Qe2 d6
lines.idea: A classic hedgehog: slow on the surface, tense underneath.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6 Nc3 Qc7 Bd3 Nc6 Be3 Nf6 O-O
lines.idea: Pressure on d4 and e4, with ...Ne5 and ...Bd6 ideas.

lines.name: Against c4
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4 Bd3 Nc6
lines.idea: ...Bb4 hits the knight defending e4.

openings.name: Sicilian: Classical
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 d6
openings.summary: Natural development and solid structure. A safe route into Sicilian waters.

lines.name: Richter-Rauzer
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 d6 Bg5 e6 Qd2 a6 O-O-O Bd7 f4 b5
lines.idea: White attacks in the centre. You answer with queenside play.

lines.name: Sozin
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 d6 Bc4 Qb6 Nb3 e6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: ...Qb6 pushes the knight back and takes the sting out of the attack.

lines.name: Against Be2
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 d6 Be2 e5 Nb3 Be7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Easy play: claim the centre with ...e5.

openings.name: Sicilian: Scheveningen
openings.prefix: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6
openings.summary: Kasparov's small-centre setup: compact, elastic and full of counterpunches.

lines.name: Against Be2
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Be2 a6 O-O Be7 Be3 O-O f4 Qc7
lines.idea: Standard setup. Your small centre controls key squares.

lines.name: Keres Attack
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 g4 h6 h4 Nc6 Rg1 h5
lines.idea: White attacks straight away. ...h6 and ...h5 fight back on that very wing.

lines.name: English Attack
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Be3 a6 f3 b5 Qd2 Bb7
lines.idea: Go for ...b5, ...b4 and ...Nbd7 as fast as you can.

openings.name: Sicilian: Handling the Anti-Sicilians
openings.summary: Half your Sicilian games never reach move 3.d4. Be ready for Alapin, Grand Prix and Morra.

lines.name: Alapin
lines.moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 cxd4 Nf3 Nc6 cxd4 d6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb5 dxe5
lines.idea: Hit the centre before White gets settled.

lines.name: Closed
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6 Nge2 e6 O-O Nge7
lines.idea: Copy the fianchetto and expand with ...Rb8 and ...b5.

lines.name: Grand Prix
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Bc4 e6 f5 Nge7
lines.idea: ...e6 and ...Ne7 cover f5 and shut down the attack on f7.

lines.name: Smith-Morra
lines.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 Bc4 e6 O-O Nf6
lines.idea: Take the pawn and develop calmly. ...e6 blunts the bishop.

lines.name: Moscow
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+ Bd7 Bxd7+ Qxd7 O-O Nc6 c3 Nf6 Re1 e6
lines.idea: Trade bishops without fear. You end up solid with control of d4.

lines.name: Open Sicilian
lines.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
lines.idea: Your Najdorf goes here. Pick your own favourite setup later.

openings.name: Caro-Kann Defence
openings.summary: Rock-solid with healthy pawns. Your bishop escapes before ...e6.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
lines.idea: Your bishop gets out before ...e6, and after the trade your pieces have easy squares.

lines.name: Advance
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nd7 O-O Ne7 Nbd2 h6
lines.idea: Get the bishop outside the chain, then undermine d4 with ...c5.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3 Qd7
lines.idea: ...Bg4 gets your bishop out before ...e6 shuts it in.

lines.name: Panov Attack
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Be7 cxd5 Nxd5
lines.idea: White has an isolated pawn. Blockade it on d5 and trade pieces.

lines.name: Two Knights
lines.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4 Nf6 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Qxd4 O-O Qd8
lines.idea: Give up the bishop, and take the d4 pawn if White offers it. Your structure is sound.

lines.name: Fantasy
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Be3 Bb4 Qd3 O-O
lines.idea: ...e6 and ...Bb4 are the calm antidote. Do not grab anything too early.

lines.name: King's Indian Attack
lines.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nd2 e5 Ngf3 Bd6 g3 Nf6 Bg2 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Take the centre with ...e5, because White has been too modest.

lines.name: Against early Nf3
lines.moves: e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4 Nf6 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Qxd4 O-O Qd8
lines.idea: Transposes straight into the Two Knights.

openings.name: French Defence
openings.summary: A firm pawn chain in exchange for a bad bishop. Counterattack the base with ...c5 and ...f6.

lines.name: Advance
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 Nh6 b4 cxd4 cxd4 Nf5
lines.idea: Throw everything at d4: ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Qb6, and the knight heads to f5.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3 Nf6 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O Bg5 Bg4
lines.idea: Symmetrical, and your c8 bishop is free. Develop just like White.

lines.name: Tarrasch
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 exd5 exd5 Ngf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bd6 dxc5 Bxc5 O-O Ne7
lines.idea: Accept the isolated pawn for active pieces and open lines.

lines.name: Winawer
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O
lines.idea: Double White's pawns at the price of the bishop pair.

lines.name: Winawer: Bd3
lines.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Nf6 Bf3 c5 Ne2 cxd4 Qxd4 Qxd4 Nxd4 O-O Bd2 Nbd7
lines.idea: Take on e4 and hit back with ...c5. With the queens off, you have no worries.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 exd5 exd5 d4 Nf6 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Transposes to the Exchange. Develop symmetrically.

lines.name: King's Indian Attack
lines.moves: e4 e6 d3 d5 Nd2 Nf6 Ngf3 c5 g3 Nc6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Occupy the centre with ...d5 and ...c5, and play on the queenside.

openings.name: Scandinavian Defence
openings.summary: Hit the centre on move one. Little theory and a Caro-Kann structure.

lines.name: Main line with ...Qa5
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 c6 Bc4 Bf5 Bd2 e6 Nd5 Qd8
lines.idea: The queen is safe on a5. ...c6 gives her a way home and ...Bf5 develops.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Nc6 d4 O-O-O
lines.idea: Castle long and pressure d4 at once.

lines.name: Against d4
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Nc6
lines.idea: Pin on f3 and normal development, with a comfortable game.

lines.name: Against e5
lines.moves: e4 d5 e5 Bf5 d4 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nc6
lines.idea: A French structure with the bishop already out: a great version for you.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 d5 Nc3 d4 Nce2 e5 Ng3 Be6 Nf3 Nc6
lines.idea: Gain space with ...d4 and ...e5 and chase the knight around.

openings.name: Scandinavian: Portuguese Gambit
openings.prefix: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4
openings.summary: Sacrifice a pawn for quick development and mating threats. Great blitz fun.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4 f3 Bf5 Bb5+ Nbd7 c4 e6 dxe6 fxe6
lines.idea: Sacrifice and develop fast: the e3 hole and White's king are your targets.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4 Nf3 Qxd5 Be2 e6 O-O Nc6
lines.idea: You win the pawn back and get a pleasant Scandinavian.

openings.name: Alekhine's Defence
openings.summary: Invite White's pawns forward, then pick them off. Hypermodern provocation.

lines.name: Modern with ...Bg4
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Be7 c4 Nb6
lines.idea: Pressure the centre with your pieces. It can collapse under its own weight.

lines.name: Four Pawns Attack
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4 dxe5 fxe5 Nc6 Be3 Bf5 Nc3 e6
lines.idea: White's pawns are big but brittle. Hit them from every side.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 exd6 exd6 Nc3 Be7 Bd3 Nc6
lines.idea: A safe structure. Your pieces develop naturally.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 e5 Nfd7 d4 e6 Nf3 c5
lines.idea: A French-style structure with your bishop still free.

lines.name: Against d3
lines.moves: e4 Nf6 d3 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Be2 d5 Nbd2 Be7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: A passive setup lets you take the centre.

openings.name: Pirc Defence
openings.summary: Let White build a centre, then strike it from a coiled position.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Be2 O-O O-O c6 h3 Nbd7
lines.idea: ...c6, ...b5 or ...e5 are all possible. Pick your moment.

lines.name: Austrian Attack
lines.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Bd3 Na6 O-O c5 d5 Nc7
lines.idea: ...c5 hits the centre. Your knight on a6 supports the queenside.

lines.name: 150 Attack
lines.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 c6 Qd2 b5 f3 Nbd7
lines.idea: Get on with ...b5 first and castle only when it is safe.

openings.name: Modern Defence
openings.summary: Just play ...g6, ...Bg7 and react. Flexible and hard to prepare against.

lines.name: Against Be3
lines.moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 Be3 a6 Qd2 b5 f3 Nd7 h4 h5
lines.idea: ...b5 and ...Bb7 hit e4. ...h5 stops the kingside storm.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Nf6 Qe2 O-O
lines.idea: Finish development, then go for ...Nc6 and ...e5.

lines.name: Against c4
lines.moves: e4 g6 d4 Bg7 c4 d6 Nc3 Nc6 Be3 e5 d5 Nce7
lines.idea: A King's Indian-style closed centre. Attack on the kingside.

openings.name: Owen's Defence
openings.summary: ...b6 and ...Bb7 target e4 from afar. Unusual and easy to surprise with.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nf6 Qe2
lines.idea: Pressure e4 and d4 at once. You need ...d6 and ...Be7 next.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Bb4 Bd3 Nf6 Qe2 d5
lines.idea: ...Bb4 and ...Nf6 keep hitting e4.

openings.name: Nimzowitsch Defence
openings.summary: A knight out in front of the c-pawn! Dare White to overextend.

lines.name: Against d4
lines.moves: e4 Nc6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nge7 O-O h6
lines.idea: A French structure, except your bishop is outside the chain.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 Nc6 Nf3 e5 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4
lines.idea: A Scotch Four Knights structure is perfectly fine.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 Nc6 Nc3 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bb4
lines.idea: ...Bb4 pins the knight and pressures e4.

openings.name: 1...e5 vs the Italian
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5
openings.summary: The most natural replies, easy plans and very little to memorise.

lines.name: Pianissimo
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O a6 Bb3 Ba7 Nbd2 O-O h3 h6
lines.idea: ...Ba7 tucks the bishop away from d4 and b4 ideas.

lines.name: Against d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4 cxd4 Bb6
lines.idea: Strike back at once with ...d5. Never let the centre roll.

lines.name: Against O-O
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Nf6 d3 d6 c3 a6
lines.idea: No problems at all. Play ...O-O, ...Ba7 and ...h6.

lines.name: Evans Gambit
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 d6 Qb3 Qd7 dxe5 Bb6
lines.idea: Take the pawn and give up the centre only on your terms.

openings.name: Two Knights Defence
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6
openings.summary: Counterattack on e4 at once. Walk through the Fried Liver safely and hit back.

lines.name: Polerio against Ng5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5+ c6 dxc6 bxc6 Be2 h6 Nf3 e4 Ne5 Bd6
lines.idea: Never play ...Nxd5! Give the pawn for rapid, active development.

lines.name: Against d3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Be7 O-O O-O Re1 d6 c3 Na5 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bc2 c5
lines.idea: Go after the bishop with ...Na5 and expand on the queenside.

lines.name: Against d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5 d5 Bb5 Ne4 Nxd4 Bd7
lines.idea: ...d5 at the right moment grabs the centre back.

openings.name: 1...e5 vs the Ruy Lopez
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6
openings.summary: The Morphy Defence: kick the bishop, castle fast and prepare for a long game.

lines.name: Closed
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Bb7
lines.idea: Chase the bishop away and castle. ...Bb7 hits e4.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O f6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 c5
lines.idea: The bishop pair compensates for your doubled pawns.

lines.name: Against d3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 d3 d6 c3 g6 O-O Bg7
lines.idea: White plays quietly, so the fianchetto is very comfortable.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6
openings.summary: The Berlin Wall: Kramnik dethroned Kasparov with it. The most solid answer at the top level.

lines.name: Berlin Wall
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bxc6 dxc6 dxe5 Nf5 Qxd8+ Kxd8
lines.idea: No queens and a slightly exposed king, but your bishop pair is rock solid.

lines.name: Rio de Janeiro
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 Re1 Nd6 Nxe5 Be7 Bf1 Nxe5 Rxe5 O-O
lines.idea: Simple equality. Your pieces are nicely developed.

lines.name: Anti-Berlin
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Bc5 c3 O-O O-O d6 Nbd2 a6 Ba4
lines.idea: White avoids the endgame. ...Bc5 sits on its best diagonal.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Attack
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5
openings.summary: Frank Marshall saved it for years to spring it on Capablanca. Sacrifice a pawn for a raging attack.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6 d4 Bd6 Re1 Qh4 g3 Qh3
lines.idea: Queen on h3, bishop on d6, and the rest of your army on the way. Bg4 and Rae8 next.

lines.name: Declined with d3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 d3 dxe4 dxe4 Qxd1 Bxd1 Bc5
lines.idea: White opts out, but you get easy equality in the endgame.

openings.name: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5
openings.summary: Hit back on move three with ...f5! A rude, risky counterattack.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6+ Qxf6 Qe2 Be7
lines.idea: Open the f-file and develop rapidly.

lines.name: Against d3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3 fxe4 dxe4 Nf6 O-O Bc5
lines.idea: A calm response lets you develop with a very comfortable game.

lines.name: Against exf5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 exf5 e4 Qe2 Qe7 Bxc6 dxc6 Nd4 Qe5
lines.idea: ...e4 is the key, and ...Qe7 keeps everything protected.

openings.name: 1...e5 vs the Scotch
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4
openings.summary: Meet the open centre head on and hit e4 and d4 straight away.

lines.name: With ...Nf6
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6 e5 Qe7 Qe2 Nd5 c4 Ba6
lines.idea: Pin the e-pawn with your queen and centralise the knight.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4 Nxc6 bxc6 Bd3 d5
lines.idea: ...Bb4 and ...d5 solve all your problems in one go.

openings.name: 1...e5 vs the Vienna
openings.summary: Be ready for the Vienna Gambit and the early queen raid on f7.

lines.name: Vienna Gambit
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 Nf3 Be7 d4 O-O Bd3 f5
lines.idea: ...d5 is the right answer to f4: the centre opens in your favour.

lines.name: Against Bc4 and Qh5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Be7 Qxe5 O-O Nf3 Nc6 Qf4 Na5
lines.idea: Take on e4, give the pawn back with ...Be7 and ...O-O, then hunt the b3 bishop.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bb4
lines.idea: A Four Knights where ...Bb4 pressures e4.

openings.name: King's Gambit Accepted
openings.summary: Take the pawn and make White prove the attack is worth it.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6 d4 g5 h4 g4 Ng1 Qf6
lines.idea: Fischer's move ...d6 is rock solid. ...g5 holds your extra pawn.

lines.name: Against Bc4
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4 Nf6 Nc3 c6 Bb3 d5 exd5 cxd5
lines.idea: Strike in the centre and develop rapidly.

lines.name: Against d4
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 d4 d5 exd5 Nf6 Bxf4 Nxd5
lines.idea: Trade off centre pawns and develop with no problems.

openings.name: Falkbeer Countergambit
openings.summary: Answer a gambit with a gambit. White's king gets exposed in a hurry.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 e4 d3 Nf6 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf3 Bc5 Qe2 Bf5 Nc3 Qe7
lines.idea: ...Bf5 protects the knight, and the pin on the e-file makes White's position awkward.

lines.name: Against exd5 exf4
lines.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxd5 O-O Be7
lines.idea: If you prefer calm, take on f4 for a good King's Gambit Accepted.

openings.name: Petrov Defence
openings.summary: Counterattack e4 rather than defend e5. A drawish reputation that hides sharp traps.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3 Nc6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: Never take on e4 straight away. Play ...d6 first, then take.

lines.name: Nimzowitsch Attack
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nc3 Nxc3 dxc3 Be7 Be3 O-O
lines.idea: Castle kingside and stay calm while White goes long.

lines.name: Steinitz
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Nd7 Nxd7 Bxd7 O-O Bd6
lines.idea: Trade pieces in the centre for an easy equal game.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O
lines.idea: You have transposed to a Four Knights.

lines.name: Against Bc4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nc3 Nxc3 dxc3 f6 Nh4 g6
lines.idea: Take on e4 and stop Nxe5 with ...f6.

openings.name: Stafford Gambit
openings.prefix: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6
openings.summary: Eric Rosen made it famous. Objectively bad, but packed with mating traps people fall for.

lines.name: Main trap line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5 Bg5 Bxf2+ Kxf2 Ng4+ Bxg4 Qxg5
lines.idea: A trap: it only works if White takes everything. Against accurate replies you are just worse.

lines.name: Against e5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 e5 Ne4 d3 Bc5 dxe4 Bxf2+ Ke2 Bg4+
lines.idea: A trap: dropping the knight is the point, because ...Bxf2+ and ...Bg4+ win the queen.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 Nc3 Bc5 Be2 h5 h3 Qd4
lines.idea: ...Qd4 eyes f2 and e4 at the same time.

openings.name: Philidor Defence
openings.summary: Solid and old-fashioned, named for the 18th-century master. A compact, safe setup.

lines.name: Hanham
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7 Bc4 Be7 O-O O-O a4 c6
lines.idea: A stubborn fortress: ...c6, ...Qc7 and ...b6 keep everything covered.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Be7 Bf4 O-O Qd2 c6
lines.idea: Space for White, but your position has no weaknesses.

lines.name: Against Bc4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Be7 O-O Nf6 d3 O-O
lines.idea: Develop quietly. White has no way to break through soon.

openings.name: Latvian Gambit
openings.summary: The most reckless second move in chess. Great for catching opponents cold.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Nxe5 Qf6 d4 d6 Nc4 fxe4 Nc3 Qg6
lines.idea: Your queen and advanced e-pawn create real threats. Be bold.

lines.name: Against exf5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 exf5 e4 Ne5 Nf6 d3 Qe7 d4 d6 Nc4 Bxf5
lines.idea: ...e4 kicks the knight, and ...Qe7 and ...d6 win back the f5 pawn.

lines.name: Against Bc4
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Bc4 fxe4 Nxe5 d5 Qh5+ g6 Nxg6 hxg6 Qxh8
lines.idea: This is the wild Svedenborg. It's sharp, so check it after the game!

openings.name: Elephant Gambit
openings.summary: Hit the centre on move two and fight for open lines right away.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Bd6 d4 e4 Ne5 Nf6 Bc4 O-O
lines.idea: Develop rapidly and get your pieces out in front of the extra pawn.

lines.name: Against Nxe5
lines.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Bc4 Qg5 d4 Qxg2 Rf1 Be6
lines.idea: ...Qg5 hits g2 and the knight at once. Accurate defence is hard.

openings.name: King's Indian Defence
openings.summary: Fischer and Kasparov's choice. Give up the centre, then storm White's king.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7
lines.idea: With the centre closed, play ...Ne8 or ...Nd7, then ...f5 and go!

lines.name: Sämisch
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3 O-O Be3 e5 d5 Nh5 Qd2 f5
lines.idea: ...e5 and ...f5 attack the centre before White castles long.

lines.name: Four Pawns
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4 O-O Nf3 c5 d5 e6 Be2 exd5
lines.idea: Attack the overextended centre from the sides.

lines.name: Fianchetto
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3 O-O Bg2 d6 O-O Nbd7 Nc3 e5
lines.idea: Set up ...e5 with support from the d7 knight.

openings.name: King's Indian vs d4 Systems
openings.summary: Half your games never see c4. Your ...g6 and ...c5 answer to the London, Colle and Torre.

lines.name: Against the London
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 e3 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Be2 d6 h3 c5 c3 Nc6
lines.idea: ...c5 and ...Qb6 hit b2 and d4: the system's classic weak spots.

lines.name: Against Nf3 and Bf4
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 O-O Be2 d6 h3 c5 c3 Nc6
lines.idea: Same plan regardless of move order.

lines.name: Against the Trompowsky
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4 c5 f3 Qa5+ c3 Nf6 d5 Qb6
lines.idea: Jump to e4 at once and go after b2.

lines.name: Against the Colle
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 e3 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O O-O d6 c4 Nc6 Nc3 e5
lines.idea: White's e3 is passive, so grab the centre with ...e5.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 a6 Nf3 Bg4
lines.idea: Without c4, take the centre with ...d5. Then ...a6 stops the Nb5 threat.

lines.name: Against c4
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5
lines.idea: Your main-line King's Indian.

openings.name: Nimzo-Indian Defence
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4
openings.summary: One of the most respected defences in chess. Pin the knight and stop e4.

lines.name: Rubinstein
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 O-O Bd3 d5 Nf3 c5 O-O Nc6 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 dxc4 Bxc4 Qc7
lines.idea: Give up the bishop to double the pawns, then attack the weak c-pawns.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 O-O a3 Bxc3+ Qxc3 b6 Bg5 Bb7
lines.idea: ...b6 and ...Bb7 fight for the e4 square.

lines.name: Sämisch
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3+ bxc3 c5 e3 Nc6 Bd3 O-O
lines.idea: Pressure the doubled c-pawns at every opportunity.

lines.name: Leningrad
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5 h6 Bh4 c5 d5 d6 e3 Bxc3+ bxc3 e5
lines.idea: Trade the bishop and close the centre for a knight-friendly game.

openings.name: Queen's Indian Defence
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6
openings.summary: Solid and elegant. The bishop takes the long diagonal and clamps down on e4.

lines.name: Fianchetto
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3 Ba6 b3 Bb4+ Bd2 Be7 Bg2 c6 O-O d5
lines.idea: ...Ba6 hits c4 and forces White to find an awkward defence.

lines.name: Petrosian
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 a3 Ba6 Qc2 Bb7 Nc3 c5 e4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6
lines.idea: Trade central pawns and use your pieces to pressure e4.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5 Bb7 e3 h6 Bh4 g5 Bg3 Ne4
lines.idea: ...Bb4 pins the knight, and ...Ne4 stops the plan cold.

openings.name: Bogo-Indian Defence
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+
openings.summary: A check to disturb White's plans. Less theory than the Nimzo with similar ideas.

lines.name: Against Bd2
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Bd2 Qe7 g3 Nc6 Bg2 Bxd2+ Nbxd2 d6 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Trade the bishop, then play ...e5 for a pleasant game.

lines.name: Against Nbd2
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 b6 a3 Bxd2+ Bxd2 Bb7 Bg5 d6
lines.idea: ...b6 and ...Bb7 take control of e4.

openings.name: Grünfeld Defence
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
openings.summary: Kasparov's favourite. Let White build a giant centre, then blow it up.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Rb1 O-O Be2 Nc6
lines.idea: Pressure the centre with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bg4. It will crack.

lines.name: Russian
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg7 Qb3 dxc4 Qxc4 O-O e4 Bg4 Be3 Nfd7
lines.idea: White's queen is exposed and the g7 bishop hits d4.

lines.name: Against Bf4
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bf4 Bg7 e3 c5 dxc5 Qa5 Rc1 dxc4 Bxc4 O-O
lines.idea: Sacrifice a pawn for a very active game.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
openings.summary: Classical and reliable for over a century. Hold d5, castle and free your game with ...c5.

lines.name: Tartakower
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 b6 cxd5 Nxd5 Bxe7 Qxe7
lines.idea: ...b6 gives your problem bishop on c8 a home.

lines.name: With Bf4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3 c5 dxc5 Bxc5
lines.idea: Break with ...c5 in time and activate the bishop.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 cxd5 exd5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Bd3 Nbd7 Nf3 Re8
lines.idea: With the structure set, your c8 bishop is no longer shut in.

lines.name: Catalan
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3 Nf6 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O dxc4 Qc2 a6 a4 Bd7
lines.idea: Take on c4 and use ...Bd7-c6 to neutralise the long diagonal.

openings.name: 1...d5 vs London & d4 Systems
openings.summary: What to do when White avoids c4. Punish the London, Colle and Jobava.

lines.name: Against the London
lines.moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Qb3 c4 Qc2 Bf5
lines.idea: ...c5 and ...Qb6 punish b2, and ...c4 grabs space.

lines.name: Against Nf3 no c4
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 c3 Qb6 Qb3 c4 Qc2 Bf5
lines.idea: Same scheme: play ...c5 and activate the queen.

lines.name: Against the Colle
lines.moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2 Bd6 O-O O-O
lines.idea: A natural plan: develop and play ...c5 before White gets e4 in.

lines.name: Against the Jobava
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 a6 Nf3 Bg4
lines.idea: Trade on d4, and play ...a6 before anything else: Nb5 is the whole point of the Jobava.

lines.name: Against the Veresov
lines.moves: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 Nf3 h6 Bh4 e6 e3 Be7
lines.idea: Defend with the knight and chase away the bishop.

lines.name: Against the Blackmar-Diemer
lines.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 g6 Bc4 Bg7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Take the pawn and fianchetto: your king is safe and you are ahead.

lines.name: Against c4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 b6
lines.idea: Your Queen's Gambit Declined.

openings.name: Slav Defence
openings.summary: Hold d5 with the c-pawn and keep the c8 bishop free. Very solid.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O
lines.idea: Take on c4 once your bishop can get out, then ...Bb4 adds pressure.

lines.name: Exchange
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4 Nc6 e3 Bf5 Nf3 e6
lines.idea: Copy the development, and you reach comfortable equality.

lines.name: With e3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Nh4 Bg6 Nxg6 hxg6
lines.idea: If you lose the bishop, the half-open h-file makes up for it.

lines.name: With Nc3 first
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Nh4 Bg6 Nxg6 hxg6
lines.idea: Transposes: the bishop came out before ...e6.

openings.name: Semi-Slav Defence
openings.prefix: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6
openings.summary: Solid-looking but explosive. Home of the Botvinnik and Meran variations.

lines.name: Meran
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5 Bd3 Bb7 O-O a6
lines.idea: ...b5 gains space with tempo, and ...c5 follows to free your game.

lines.name: Botvinnik
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5 Nxg5 hxg5 Bxg5 Nbd7
lines.idea: One of the sharpest lines in all of chess. Study it after every game!

lines.name: Moscow
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bxf6 Qxf6 e3 Nd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 g6
lines.idea: You keep the bishop pair and a solid structure.

openings.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
openings.summary: Take the pawn, then give it back for free piece play and a clear plan.

lines.name: Classical
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O a6 a4 Nc6
lines.idea: Strike at d4 with ...c5, and develop calmly.

lines.name: Against e4
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e5 Nf3 exd4 Bxc4 Nc6 O-O Be6
lines.idea: ...e5 immediately hits the centre.

lines.name: Against e3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 e6 Nf3 c5 O-O a6
lines.idea: Transposes to the main line.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nc3 e5 d5 Nf6 e4 b5 Nxb5 Nxe4 Nc3 Nxc3 bxc3 Nd7
lines.idea: ...b5 gives back a pawn to win e4, and White's structure ends up damaged.

openings.name: Tarrasch Defence
openings.prefix: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5
openings.summary: Accept an isolated pawn for free, active pieces. Kasparov played it as a junior.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5 exd5 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O
lines.idea: All your pieces come out easily. The d5 pawn is strong as well as weak.

lines.name: Against e3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 e3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 cxd5 exd5 Bb5 Bd6
lines.idea: You have free development and no problems at all.

lines.name: Schara Gambit
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5 cxd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qd1 exd5 Qxd5 Be6
lines.idea: A gambit: give a pawn for a large lead in development.

openings.name: Dutch: Leningrad
openings.summary: Combine the Dutch with a King's Indian bishop. Direct attacking chances.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6 Nf3 Bg7 O-O O-O c4 d6 Nc3 Qe8
lines.idea: Fianchetto, then ...Qe8 prepares ...e5 with force.

lines.name: With c4 first
lines.moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3 O-O Bg2 d6 O-O Qe8
lines.idea: Move order does not matter: a Leningrad with ...e5 next.

lines.name: Against Bg5
lines.moves: d4 f5 Bg5 h6 Bh4 g5 Bg3 Nf6 e3 d6
lines.idea: Chase the bishop without fear and gain kingside space.

lines.name: Staunton Gambit
lines.moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 c6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 d5
lines.idea: Accept and consolidate with ...c6 and ...d5: you keep the pawn.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: d4 f5 Nf3 Nf6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 O-O O-O c4 d6
lines.idea: The same Leningrad setup.

lines.name: Against Bf4
lines.moves: d4 f5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Be2 O-O
lines.idea: White avoids the fight, so finish your development.

openings.name: Dutch: Stonewall
openings.prefix: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5
openings.summary: Lock down e4 with a wall of pawns. Carlsen has played it against the very best.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5 Nf3 c6 O-O Bd6 b3 Qe7
lines.idea: Stop Ba3 with ...Qe7 and plan ...Nbd7 and ...Ne4.

lines.name: Against Nh3
lines.moves: d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5 Nh3 c6 O-O Bd6 b3 Qe7
lines.idea: The knight heads for f4. Your setup does not change.

openings.name: Modern Benoni
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6
openings.summary: Fischer stunned Spassky with it. Imbalanced from the start: dynamic play for both sides.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 e4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 Be2 O-O O-O Re8
lines.idea: Your queenside majority and the g7 bishop are your hopes.

lines.name: Fianchetto
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 Nf3 g6 g3 Bg7 Bg2 O-O O-O a6
lines.idea: ...a6, ...Nbd7 and ...b5 give you queenside play.

openings.name: Benko Gambit
openings.prefix: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5
openings.summary: A true positional gambit: long-lasting pressure with no queens needed.

lines.name: Accepted
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6 Bxa6 Nc3 d6 e4 Bxf1 Kxf1 g6
lines.idea: White's king is misplaced. Your rooks own the a- and b-files.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 Nf3 g6 cxb5 a6 bxa6 Bxa6
lines.idea: The same setup. Your long-term pressure stays.

openings.name: Budapest Gambit
openings.summary: A surprise on move two. White's pieces get tangled up and tricks abound.

lines.name: Rubinstein
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2 Qe7 a3 Ngxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5
lines.idea: Win the pawn back while White's pieces trip over one another.

lines.name: Alekhine
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 e4 Nxe5 f4 Nec6
lines.idea: White's big centre is loose. Hit it with ...Bc5 and ...d6.

lines.name: Fajarowicz trick
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Nf3 Bc5 e3 Nc6
lines.idea: ...Bc5 aims at f2, and you collect e5 later.

openings.name: Albin Countergambit
openings.summary: Strike the Queen's Gambit right back. Home of the famous Lasker Trap.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 g3 Be6 Nbd2 Qd7 Bg2 O-O-O
lines.idea: The d4 wedge cramps White. Castle long and play ...Bh3.

lines.name: Lasker Trap
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+
lines.idea: An underpromotion to a knight wins! The most beautiful trap in the book.

openings.name: Englund Gambit
openings.summary: A cheeky blitz trap. Objectively unsound, but one wrong move and it's mate.

lines.name: The famous trap
lines.moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3 Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1#
lines.idea: Back-rank mate on c1. It works alarmingly often.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Nc3 Nxe5 Nd5 Nxf3+ gxf3 Qd8
lines.idea: You win the pawn back. Your position is fine.

lines.name: Against e4
lines.moves: d4 e5 e4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qe3 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4
lines.idea: A Center Game. Gain time on the queen and develop quickly.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: d4 e5 Nf3 e4 Ne5 d6 Nc4 d5 Ne3 Nf6
lines.idea: ...e4 and ...d6 chase the knight around.

openings.name: Chigorin Defence
openings.summary: Break every classical rule: block the c-pawn and go for rapid piece play.

lines.name: Against Nf3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Bxf3 gxf3 Qxd5 e3 e5 Nc3 Bb4
lines.idea: White has two bishops but a ruined structure. Keep it closed.

lines.name: Against cxd5
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 cxd5 Qxd5 e3 e5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 Bxc3
lines.idea: ...e5 hits d4 immediately, with lots of piece activity.

lines.name: Against Nc3
lines.moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 Nc3 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e4 Bg4 Be3 e6
lines.idea: Grab the pawn and build pressure on d4.

openings.name: Old Indian Defence
openings.summary: A sturdy King's Indian relative where your bishop stays on e7.

lines.name: Main line
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 d6 Nc3 e5 Nf3 Nbd7 e4 Be7 Be2 O-O O-O c6
lines.idea: Solid and flexible. ...Re8, ...Bf8 and ...a6 are all part of the plan.

lines.name: Against g3
lines.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 d6 Nf3 Nbd7 g3 e5 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O Nc3 c6
lines.idea: Same setup and same ideas.

openings.name: 1...e5 vs the English
openings.summary: A Sicilian with colours reversed: seize the centre and play with clear plans.

lines.name: Four Knights
lines.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2 Nb6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: Grab the centre with ...d5 and prepare a solid development.

lines.name: With e3
lines.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 e3 Bb4 Qc2 O-O d3 Re8
lines.idea: ...Bb4 and ...Re8 prepare ...e4.

lines.name: Fianchetto
lines.moves: c4 e5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Nc3 Nb6 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: Same plan: ...d5, then drop the knight back to b6.

lines.name: With Nc3 and g3
lines.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2 Nb6 Nf3 Nc6 O-O Be7
lines.idea: Transposes to the main scheme.
